Nonnegative shifted form q_H[u]−v*||u||²=||uʹ||²+int_H(V−v*)|u|² gives lambda(H)>=v* for every connected cluster. k disjoint Dirichlet intervals of length L on any lowest-potential ray give max eigenvalue v*+pi²/L² ->v*, establishing the infimum for every k. A lowest-potential tail gives lambda(H)=Sigma(H)=v* by Weyl/test functions and Persson; a cluster without such tail has bounded geometry or asymptotic potential >v*, so any lambda=v* would be an L² eigenfunction. Equality in the shifted form forces derivative zero and support only on minimum-potential pieces, incompatible with a nonzero L² vector on the connected cluster, excluding this possibility. Distinct minimizing clusters need distinct nonoverlapping min-ray tails, so k<=r; choosing k low tails attains. The exact non-covering convention is essential.
